commitResults.messageBody:
Java classes have inconsistent imports, documentation, and mutable
implementation details that make the code harder to review.

Apply consistent layout, final fields, explicit imports, and public API
Javadocs. Correct task-list copying and task-index retention to improve
type safety and ensure the selected task is updated. Add regression
coverage for both behaviors.

Java style guidance is not stored in the project, so code reviews can
apply the conventions inconsistently.

Add a project-specific skill based on the SE-EDU Java standard and track
its files so future agents can load the same rules.

Commit and branch conventions are not stored in the project, so commit
history can become inconsistent across contributors.

Add a project-specific skill based on the SE-EDU Git conventions so
future commit messages and branch names follow a shared standard.

Project instructions do not explicitly require the project-specific Java
and Git standards during future work.

Require agents to follow both skills for code changes and commit
preparation so project conventions are applied consistently.

Claude-specific instructions only reference AGENTS.md and omit the
project-specific coding and commit standards.

Add explicit Java and Git standard requirements so Claude sessions
follow the same rules as other project agents.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for internal task invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Document assumptions that parser, command, task,
task list, storage and GUI depend on. Detect null
state and unexpected task-list mutations early
during development.

Kepe invalid user input on the existing
ChudException handling, since assertions may be
disabled. Add unit tests covering the asserted task
and task list construction constraints.

The saved-task parser currently validates record structure, decodes the
completion status, selects a task type, and constructs that task in one
method. This mixes abstraction levels and makes malformed-record handling
difficult to follow.

Separate completion-status parsing and task construction into focused
helpers. Use an explicit switch for the finite task types so the main
parsing flow reads as validation, construction, and status application.

Add focused load tests for every supported task type and representative
malformed records. This protects the behavior-preserving refactoring and
documents the intended tolerance of invalid saved data.

Indexed task operations currently repeat the same bounds condition. This
duplication makes the list harder to scan and creates several places that
must remain synchronized when validation rules change.

Move the bounds check into one focused helper and name the existing error
messages as constants. Preserve each operation's current exception text so
the refactoring does not alter observable behavior.

Strengthen the invalid-update test to verify that rejected indexes leave
both the selected task and the list unchanged.

Use stream collectors to format task lists and saved task records.
This avoids repeated string concatenation and prevents an unwanted leading
line separator in the save file.

Simplify task filtering with Stream.toList() and clarify its documentation.
Add assertions for internal task invariants
Improve code quality
TaskList: Streamline task formatting
